card.title: iPhone 15 Pro/Pro Max Random Restarts Traced to Panic Logs and Flex Sensors

source.title: How To Fix an iPhone 15 Pro That Randomly Restarts - Repair Wiki

symptoms: After a back glass repair, the iPhone will restart on its ow
After a hard drop, the iPhone will restart every 3 minutes
After a screen repair, the iPhone will bootloop every 3 minu
After replacing the charging port flex, the device will auto
The iPhone will reboot randomly when using it
The iPhone will seem to freeze and restart every 2-5 minutes

claims.statement: Unplugged or defective proximity flex causes restarts associated with panic log error 0x200000.
claims.evidence: OS panic log file indicates SMC PANIC - ASSERTION FAILED referencing the sensor array.

claims.statement: Charging port flex issues trigger panic log errors 0x300000 or 0x100000.
claims.evidence: Device restarts every 3 minutes if the charging port flex is unplugged or damaged.

claims.statement: Wireless charging flex on the back glass being unplugged or damaged causes panic log error 0x400000.
claims.evidence: Panic log generated when the wireless charging flex is disconnected.
claims.quote: 0x400000 (and or 4194304) - It's the Wireless Charging Flex on the Back Glass

claims.statement: Simultaneous proximity flex and wireless charging flex faults trigger panic log error 0x600000.
claims.evidence: Panic log indicates sensor array assertion failure covering multiple disconnected or damaged peripherals.
claims.quote: 0x600000 (or 6291456)- It's 2 problems, the Proximity Flex and Wireless Charging Flex

claims.statement: Combined charging port flex and wireless charging flex issues result in panic log error 0x700000.
claims.evidence: Both flex cables cause a multi-sensor assertion failure in the panic log.
claims.quote: 0x700000 (or 7340032)- It's 2 problems: Charging Port Flex and Wireless Charging Flex

claims.statement: Battery data issues or defective batteries trigger panic log error 0xa1.
claims.evidence: Symptoms include fluctuating battery percentage, non-genuine battery messages, and 3-minute restart loops.

procedure: Navigate to Settings, Privacy, Analytics & Improvements, and Analytics Data on the device.
Locate and open the most recent panic-full log file.
Scan the panic log text for SMC PANIC - ASSERTION FAILED and check the hexadecimal error code.
Inspect the corresponding flex cable or battery connector for damage, liquid damage, or improper seating.
Perform diode mode measurements on the FPC connectors or battery connector pins to check for faults against a known good board.
cautions: SOURCE RISK: Do not attempt to test the device with essential flex cables unplugged, as the phone will continuously restart by design.
card.caveats: Panic log analysis tools only provide suggestions and are not infallible official diagnostic lists from Apple.
